newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurotunnel adds up fire costs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurotunnel adds up fire costs.

text.p: Debt-laden Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA said on Wednesday revenues were back on track after last November's fire, with turnover so far this year running in line with forecasts in its huge loan restructuring plan.

Eurotunnel said service interruptions caused by the fire cut turnover to 168.8 million pounds ($266.5 million) in the first six months of 1997, from 223.6 million in the first half of 1996, but compensation received from its fire insurance adds 52.4 million pounds to the reported first-half turnover figure this year.

Sales in the second quarter rose to 93.3 million pounds from 75.5 million pounds in the first three months, before insurance receipts of 28.9 million pounds in the first quarter, 23.5 million pounds in the second.
Including the insurance receipts, Eurotunnel said the first-half total of 221.2 million pounds was in line with upper forecasts in its debt restructuring prospectus.

The Anglo-French firm is due to seek final approvals from its banks later this year for the proposals to restructure nearly nine billion pounds of debt through an equity swap, having won shareholder backing last month.
The plan is designed to cut interest charges to around 330 million pounds this year from 580 million paid in 1996, but will cut shareholders' equity to 54.5 percent, giving the banks 45.5 percent.

French chairman Patrick Ponsolle told shareholders last month that Eurotunnel expected to show a loss after interest of 2.72 billion francs this year, less than half the 1996 loss of 6.1 billion francs.
Eurotunnel's freight truck service was closed for seven months following last year's blaze, which broke out on one of the open-sided truck wagons, only reopening to commercial traffic on June 15.
Last week Eurotunnel said Le Shuttle Freight service carried 36,491 trucks in July, its first full month back in operation, compared with 53,978 in July 1996.
Meanwhile the number of vehicles using its Le Shuttle Tourist service for cars and coaches in July rose 29.5 percent to 234,073 versus June, which it said was almost back to its July 1996 level.
Traffic on the independently-operated Eurostar inter-city passenger service hit an all-time high in July with 651,849 passengers, up 24 percent on June and 23 percent on July 1996.

Tonnage carried by freight trains in July slipped three percent to 266,345 tonnes due to seasonal variations versus June, but that number was still 24 percent higher than July 1996, the company said. ($ = 0.633 British Pounds)
